decision: Runner and independent accounting qualify for the declared full comparison; original process remains running. No full-workload benefit, collector adoption or deployment decision yet.
falsifier: A changed original payload/deadline, omitted attempt, fabricated client arrival or acknowledgement, corrupted accepted accounting, or incomplete full comparison prevents a benefit claim. Newly late/unavailable data counts against adoption.
hypothesis: Full physical collector-path replay can quantify whether duplicate-call savings survive process startup, queue, delivery and correlated-failure costs under explicit timing consent.
limitations: Full original-speed comparison remains running; unit/control results are not complete workload benefit evidence.
Historical trace and leader bytes/durations are fixed development inputs; adaptive replanning/retries and changing venue responses remain unqualified.
Earlier-time sharing is explicit proposed consent, not a current collector assumption.
Unknown external IP traffic, rate-limit feedback and error charges preclude global headroom claims; no quota was installed.
Synthetic failure fanout demonstrates lost follower availability; tested transport correctness does not establish financial benefit.
New research modules have 86.96% combined statement/branch coverage; input/accounting paths are fully covered, broader process/CLI guards are not.
Original ten-second deadlines and candle-freshness proxy are distinct; neither proves per-observation economic availability.
Dynamic listener, long-run resource retention, collector adapter and study continuity still need qualification before a concrete approval request.
